label: Formulated Incan moral rationalism, solar cosmology, and Quechua humanism
description: Inca Garcilaso de la Vega demonstrated that the Incan Empire constituted a sophisticated moral and civil society whose worship of the sun led naturally to the philosophical conception of Pachacamac, the invisible divine creator, proving that indigenous peoples were fully rational agents.
historicalContext: Composed in Córdoba, Spain, in 1609 by the son of an Inca princess (Chimpu Ocllo) and a Spanish conquistador.
dialecticalTension: Contrasts with Spanish scholastic justifications of conquest that depicted indigenous Americans as natural slaves lacking reason.

citations.author: Inca Garcilaso de la Vega
citations.quote: The Incas by the natural light of reason arrived at the knowledge of one God, creator of all things, whom they named Pachacamac.

citations.author: Margarita Zamora
citations.work: Language, Authority, and Indigenous History in the Comentarios reales de los incas

label: Integrated Renaissance Neoplatonism to interpret Incan metaphysics
description: Garcilaso's first major publication was the acclaimed Spanish translation of León Hebreo's Dialoghi d'Amore (1590); he subsequently utilized Hebreo's Neoplatonic metaphysics of cosmic love and harmony to systematically interpret Incan social and theological institutions.
historicalContext: The flowering of Italian and Iberian Renaissance Neoplatonism in the late 16th century.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes classical Mediterranean Neoplatonism with indigenous Andean dual-gendered solar cosmology.

citations.author: Enrique Pupo-Walker
citations.work: Historia, creación y profecía en los textos del Inca Garcilaso de la Vega

label: Provided historical proof of pre-Columbian communitarian ethics
description: Dussel frequently draws upon Garcilaso's documentation of Incan communal economics (ayllu, mita, and social provisioning) to prove that indigenous American civilizations developed sophisticated communitarian ethical systems prior to European modernity.
historicalContext: The recovery of indigenous economic ethics in 20th-century Latin American political philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Reclaims pre-capitalist Incan agrarian solidarity as a normative resource for contemporary decolonial ethics.

citations.author: Enrique Dussel
citations.work: Para una ética de la liberación latinoamericana
citations.quote: The Inca Garcilaso shows us that the Andean world was not an ethical vacuum, but a highly developed moral community oriented to the preservation of life.
